subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw add this six-event AI-safety taxonomy and permanent plugin emission contract, and should `safetyEventTypes` be informational provenance metadata or a genuinely operator-enforced authorization policy?
rationale: The repository currently treats installed plugins as trusted code, while this PR describes a self-declared manifest field as an enforcement boundary and expands compatibility-sensitive plugin APIs; code review cannot choose that permanent product and trust model.

options.title: Use provenance-first telemetry
options.body: Sponsor a host-injected emitter that validates payloads and records plugin identity and untrusted provenance without claiming self-declared manifest metadata prevents malicious plugin behavior.

options.title: Design operator authorization
options.body: Require an explicit operator-controlled allowlist or equivalent host policy before external plugin safety events are accepted, with upgrade and administrative UX defined.

options.title: Pause the taxonomy series
options.body: Keep the existing diagnostics and security event surfaces until maintainers have a concrete consumer and stable taxonomy that warrants new core and plugin contracts.

recommendation.title: Use provenance-first telemetry
recommendation.body: Sponsor a host-injected emitter that validates payloads and records plugin identity and untrusted provenance without claiming self-declared manifest metadata prevents malicious plugin behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most strongly connects this person to plugin runtime ownership and metadata-driven extension boundaries.
